target_customer: Pharma and biotech partners and relapsed or refractory blood cancer patients; later drug developers via a clinical pipeline
problem: Patients with relapsed or refractory blood cancer run out of standard options; the company tested drug combinations on each patient's own cancer cells to find ones that kill cancer and spare healthy cells.
business_model: Ex vivo drug testing services for pharma partnerships and patients, later a clinical stage drug developer after a reverse merger

founders.name: Matthew De Silva
founders.background_notes: Not verified beyond the YC page and 2019 press quotes.

founders.name: Pete Quinzio
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page; not verified further.

exit.reason: Paused its planned Phase 2 volasertib study in September 2024, cut staff, then filed for bankruptcy in October 2024

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires robust ex vivo assays on primary patient cells, lab automation and clinical validation that drug sensitivity predicts patient response, which was unproven at founding.

defensibility.rationale: Assay data from patient samples could compound, but ex vivo sensitivity testing is an academic technique other firms could replicate, and clinical validation is expensive.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought the approach; the company reverse merged into public shell VBL Therapeutics in October 2023 and went bankrupt in October 2024.

market_need_then: Relapsed and refractory blood cancers had poor outcomes and few options. Specific 2015 demand evidence was not found beyond the company's own description.

branding.domain_note: Uses notablelabs.com; domain history not found

rebrands.why: The public shell VBL took the Notable name after the reverse merger

brand_strength.rationale: Little evidence of brand awareness beyond biotech and VC press; a generic dictionary name that is easy to confuse with unrelated companies.

pivots.from: Personalized ex vivo drug combination testing platform
pivots.to: Clinical stage oncology drug developer built around volasertib licensed from Boehringer Ingelheim
pivots.why: Reverse merger with VBL Therapeutics to access public markets and fund clinical work

outcome_analysis: Notable Labs raised a $14.8M Series A in 2017 and a $40M Series B in 2019 on a personalized blood cancer drug testing platform, then pivoted through a 2023 reverse merger with VBL Therapeutics toward a clinical drug candidate. With little cash in a tough biotech funding market, it paused the volasertib Phase 2 study in September 2024, cut staff and filed for bankruptcy in October 2024.
notes: Directory status says Public but the public entity filed for bankruptcy in October 2024 (chapter 7 filings reported). The company website failed DNS lookup at fetch time. Cause of failure is partly inferred from announcements: study paused, layoffs and bankruptcy; the exact cash position was not verified.
